criteria.name: correct-severity
criteria.anchor: 1.0: critical or high. 0.5: medium. 0.0: low or informational.

criteria.name: actionable-fix
criteria.anchor: 1.0: names both the bind revert and a remote-address or server-side owner derivation. 0.5: names only one. 0.0: vague.

expected_outcomes: Finds authentication bypass: with the listener now bound to all interfaces, any network client can send X-Operator-Id and act as any owner because loopback mode trusts the header
Explains that neither hunk is exploitable alone and the flaw is the combination of the Listen change and the header trust that assumed a loopback-only bind
Recommends reverting the bind to 127.0.0.1 and not trusting the header based on config mode; verify the connection's remote address (or derive the owner server-side as loopbackowner does)
